candidates.title: Incremental background output can consume an unfinished UTF8 tail before its remaining bytes arrive
candidates.trigger: A valid overall UTF8 process stream is split across data events, and an ordinary BashOutput incremental peek occurs after a partial character prefix but before the remaining bytes; retained new output is at most the16KiB cap.
candidates.cause: onData writes original Buffer chunks into RingFile. For rawBuf.length <= READ_RETURN_CAP no safe cut is applied. toString(utf8) decodes the unfinished tail, then agentReadOffset advances by its complete byte count; later bytes cannot be rejoined for incremental output.
candidates.impact: Static inference: replacement text and loss of the original character across successive incremental reads. Full retained snapshot may still recover the original after completion if bytes remain; no disk corruption or permanent raw-buffer loss claimed.
candidates.ordinaryEntry: BashOutput definition explicitly advertises a STILL-RUNNING on-demand peek; default incremental directly calls the manager readOutput.
candidates.validation: No runtime/Buffer/stream/language fixture, shell or product test executed. Current host cross-character data event scheduling and peek timing were not observed.
candidates.classificationLimit: Strong source-level candidate retained pending direct runtime evidence; no new formal finding. Independent review keeps same adjacent lead unclassified; Root owns candidate classification.
exclusions: Not the complete valid-buffer16KiB helper cut: that ordinary helper path had no new counterexample.
NaN/fractional caps, arbitrary invalid Buffer input, ring wrap and all-snapshot UTF16 slicing are outside this item.
Historical exact-tail cause search found no matching record in stated inventory; regex search is not semantic exhaustion.
